items.title: US fires Tomahawk from Typhon launcher in Philippines for the first time

featured_image.name: US Army fires Tomahawk missile from new Typhon launcher during Philippines  drill

items.description:
The U.S. Army fired a Tomahawk cruise missile from its Typhon mid-range capability system on Philippine soil for the first time early Tuesday, launching from Tacloban City Airport on Leyte Island and striking a target roughly 600 kilometers (about 370 miles) away at Fort Magsaysay in Laur, Nueva Ecija, on the island of Luzon.[1][2][3]

The test came as China responded with a show of force over the disputed South China Sea, deploying H-6 bombers and J-16 fighter jets over Scarborough Shoal in what Beijing called "combat readiness" patrols.[4][5]

items.title: Cargo vessel hit in Strait of Hormuz amid US 'Project Freedom' launch

featured_image.name: Cargo vessel struck by projectile at Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says | Reuters

items.description: A cargo vessel was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, according to a report from the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency, Reuters reported. The attack marks the latest in a string of maritime incidents in one of the world's most critical shipping lanes, as the United States pursues a new military initiative to reopen the waterway.[1]

items.title: Rubio calls Israel-Lebanon peace 'imminently achievable'

featured_image.name: Rubio says Israel-Lebanon peace deal is achievable but Hezbollah is a  problem | Reuters

items.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared Tuesday that a peace deal between Israel and Lebanon is "imminently achievable," while identifying Hezbollah as the central obstacle to any lasting agreement between the two nations.

"By and large, I think a peace deal between Lebanon and Israel is imminently achievable, and should be," Rubio told reporters at a White House press briefing. "The problem with Israel and Lebanon is not Israel or Lebanon, it's Hezbollah."[1][2]

items.title: Rubio says Taiwan will come up at Trump-Xi summit next week

featured_image.name: Tough talk on Taiwan - GZERO Media

items.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed on Tuesday that Taiwan will be a topic of discussion when President Donald Trump meets Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 14-15, warning against any "destabilizing" actions regarding the self-governing island as the high-stakes summit approaches.

"I'm sure Taiwan will be a topic of conversation; it always is," Rubio said during a White House press briefing, adding that neither Washington nor Beijing has an interest in seeing instability in the Indo-Pacific region.[1][2][3]

items.title: Russia, Ukraine declare competing ceasefires after drone hits Moscow tower

featured_image.name: Ukrainian drone hits upmarket Moscow high-rise ahead of Victory Day  celebrations

items.description: A Ukrainian drone slammed into a luxury high-rise residential tower in southwestern Moscow early Monday, breaching the Russian capital's air defenses in one of the most brazen strikes on the city since the full-scale war began. The attack came just five days before Russia's annual Victory Day parade on May 9 and hours before Moscow declared a unilateral ceasefire for the holiday.

items.title: Pentagon says Iran attacks on US forces 'below threshold' to restart war

featured_image.name: Hegseth: US to 'stay ready' after Iran ceasefire, claims victory

items.description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth declared Tuesday that the US-Iran ceasefire remains intact despite a sharp escalation of hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz, telling reporters at a Pentagon press briefing that "the ceasefire is not over" even as Iran has attacked American forces more than 10 times since the truce began on April 7.[1]

Gen. Dan Caine, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, said the attacks remain "below the threshold for recommencing significant combat operations," adding that Iran has also fired on commercial vessels nine times and seized two container ships during the ceasefire period. "The decision to restart operations is a political one beyond my authority," Caine said. "Currently, what we are experiencing is minor harassing fire. It seems as though Iran is clutching at straws".[1]

items.title: Iran's nuclear timeline unchanged despite war, US intel finds

featured_image.name: Satellite image shows Fordow nuclear facility after massive bomb strike

items.description: Two months into a U.S.-led military campaign against Iran, American intelligence assessments indicate that the time Tehran would need to build a nuclear weapon has not shifted since last summer, when a joint U.S.-Israeli strike extended the timeline to roughly nine months to a year, Reuters reported on Monday, citing three sources familiar with the matter.[1][2]

items.title: Zelensky declares Ukraine ceasefire starting May 5-6

featured_image.name: Zelensky says Ukraine is ready for direct talks with Russia, but only after  a ceasefire

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Monday that Ukraine will observe a unilateral ceasefire beginning at midnight on the night of May 5-6, moving ahead without a formal agreement from Moscow. Writing on Telegram, Zelensky stated that Ukraine is proceeding because "human life is incomparably more valuable than the celebration of any anniversary," and that Ukraine will "act symmetrically" from the moment the ceasefire takes effect — echoing language he used during Ukraine's observance of an Orthodox Easter truce in April.[1][2]

The announcement comes hours after Russia's Defense Ministry declared its own two-day ceasefire for May 8-9 to coincide with the 81st anniversary of Victory Day, which commemorates the Soviet Union's defeat of Nazi Germany. The Kremlin said it did not require Ukraine's consent and threatened a "massive missile strike on the center of Kyiv" if Ukrainian forces attempted to disrupt the celebrations.[3][4]
